# Render-to-Texture Security Camera (Godot 4)

## Background

Build a render-to-texture security camera system in Godot 4. A separate `SubViewport` containing its own `Camera3D` renders a small 3D world; a HUD `TextureRect` displays that `SubViewport`'s `ViewportTexture` in real time, like a CCTV monitor. Repositioning the source camera at runtime must change what the monitor shows on the next rendered frame.

## Requirements

Deliver a Godot 4 project located at `/home/user/myproject` containing a valid `project.godot` for Godot 4 that the verifier can load headlessly. The project must declare a main scene in the project settings (`application/run/main_scene`). This main scene must contain all required nodes wired together, and a script (attached to the scene root) exposing the public API listed below.

Required node paths (relative to the main scene root):

* `World/SourceViewport` — a `SubViewport`.
* `World/SourceViewport/SourceCamera` — a `Camera3D` that is the current camera for the SubViewport.
* `World/SourceViewport/SceneRoot` — a `Node3D` that holds the three colored target meshes.
* `World/SourceViewport/SceneRoot/RedCube` — `MeshInstance3D`.
* `World/SourceViewport/SceneRoot/GreenCube` — `MeshInstance3D`.
* `World/SourceViewport/SceneRoot/BlueCube` — `MeshInstance3D`.
* `HUD/MonitorScreen` — a `TextureRect` whose `texture` is the `ViewportTexture` of `World/SourceViewport`.

Required public method on the main scene root script:

* `set_camera_pose(pos: Vector3, basis: Basis) -> void` — sets the global transform of `World/SourceViewport/SourceCamera` so that the next rendered frame uses this pose.

The three colored cubes must be visible as solid colors regardless of lighting:

* `RedCube` at world position `(3, 0, 0)` shown as pure red `Color(1, 0, 0)`.
* `GreenCube` at world position `(-3, 0, 0)` shown as pure green `Color(0, 1, 0)`.
* `BlueCube` at world position `(0, 0, -3)` shown as pure blue `Color(0, 0, 1)`.
  The SubViewport background (visible behind/around the cubes) must be black `Color(0, 0, 0)`.

SubViewport behavior:

* `size` must be `Vector2i(256, 256)`.
* `render_target_update_mode` must be `SubViewport.UPDATE_ALWAYS` so the texture refreshes every frame.
* `transparent_bg` must be off (false), so the background contributes the chosen clear color.

## Implementation Hints

* The render-to-texture pipeline in Godot 4 uses `SubViewport` + `ViewportTexture`. A `TextureRect` can display a `ViewportTexture` whose `viewport_path` points to the `SubViewport`.
* To get deterministic pixel colors regardless of lighting, use unshaded materials on the target meshes (for example via `StandardMaterial3D` with `shading_mode = SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED`, or by using a flat material that ignores lights).
* A solid background color for the SubViewport can be enforced via a `WorldEnvironment` placed inside the SubViewport with `Environment.background_mode = BG_COLOR` and `background_color = Color.BLACK`.
* The source camera must be the SubViewport's current camera so that `ViewportTexture.get_image()` reflects the rendered scene. Use `Camera3D.current = true` or `Camera3D.make_current()`.
* After moving the camera, the texture only reflects the new view on the *next* rendered frame; the verifier handles awaiting `RenderingServer.frame_post_draw`.
* The verifier will test your camera implementation by positioning it to look at each cube and checking the center pixel `(128, 128)` of the `SubViewport` (with a channel tolerance ≤ 0.15):
  * Looking at `RedCube`: After calling `set_camera_pose(Vector3(3, 0, 5), Basis.IDENTITY)`, the center pixel must be red-dominant (red channel ≥ 0.8, green ≤ 0.2, blue ≤ 0.2).
  * Looking at `GreenCube`: After calling `set_camera_pose(Vector3(-3, 0, 5), Basis.IDENTITY)`, the center pixel must be green-dominant (green ≥ 0.8, red ≤ 0.2, blue ≤ 0.2).
  * Looking at `BlueCube`: After calling `set_camera_pose(Vector3(0, 0, -8), Basis.from_euler(Vector3(0, PI, 0)))`, the center pixel must be blue-dominant (blue ≥ 0.8, red ≤ 0.2, green ≤ 0.2).
  * Background Check: A pixel sampled in an empty corner of the SubViewport (e.g., `(8, 8)`) must read as black (all channels ≤ 0.1) for at least one of the camera poses, proving the SubViewport background is black.

extends Node3D

# Public API: Set the source camera's global transform.
# This determines what the SubViewport renders for the security-camera monitor.
#
# Parameters:
#   pos   - world-space position of the source camera.
#   basis - world-space basis (rotation) of the source camera.
func set_camera_pose(pos: Vector3, basis: Basis) -> void:
	var source_camera: Camera3D = $World/SourceViewport/SourceCamera
	if source_camera == null:
		push_error("set_camera_pose: SourceCamera node not found at World/SourceViewport/SourceCamera")
		return
	var t := Transform3D(basis, pos)
	source_camera.global_transform = t
	# Make sure this camera stays the active camera of the SubViewport so the
	# texture reflects its view on the next rendered frame.
	source_camera.current = true
EOF

	if main == null:

		quit(1)

		"HUD",
		"HUD/MonitorScreen",
	]
	for p in required_paths:
		if not main.has_node(p):
			print("FAIL: Missing node %s" % p)
		else:
			print("OK: Found node %s (%s)" % [p, main.get_node(p).get_class()])

	# Verify types
	var sv = main.get_node("World/SourceViewport")
	print("SourceViewport class: %s, is SubViewport: %s, size: %s, transparent_bg: %s, update_mode: %d" %

	var cam = main.get_node("World/SourceViewport/SourceCamera")
	print("SourceCamera class: %s, is Camera3D: %s, current: %s" % [cam.get_class(), cam is Camera3D, cam.current])
	var monitor = main.get_node("HUD/MonitorScreen")
	print("MonitorScreen class: %s, is TextureRect: %s, has texture: %s" %
		[monitor.get_class(), monitor is TextureRect, monitor.texture != null])

	# Add scene to tree

	# Wait one frame for SubViewport to initialize
	await process_frame

	# Test set_camera_pose
	print("=== Testing set_camera_pose ===")
	main.set_camera_pose(Vector3(3, 0, 5), Basis.IDENTITY)

	print("Camera position after set_camera_pose: %s (expected (3, 0, 5))" % str(pos))

	# Test the method exists
	if main.has_method("set_camera_pose"):
		print("OK: set_camera_pose method exists")
	else:
		print("FAIL: set_camera_pose method does not exist")

	# Wait a few frames for rendering
	for i in range(5):
		await process_frame

	# Try to get image from the SubViewport texture
	var tex = sv.get_texture()
	print("SubViewport texture: %s" % tex)
	if tex != null:
		var img = tex.get_image()
		if img:
			print("Image size: %s" % str(img.get_size()))
			# Sample center pixel
			var px = img.get_pixel(128, 128)
			print("Center pixel (128,128): %s" % str(px))
			# Sample corner
			var corner = img.get_pixel(8, 8)
			print("Corner pixel (8,8): %s" % str(corner))
		else:
			print("Could not get image (dummy driver?)")

	print("=== Test complete ===")
	quit(0)
EOF

	# RedCube at (3,0,0): direction = (3,0,0) - (3,0,5) = (0,0,-5), looking down -Z. Yes!

	# Test 2: GreenCube
	main.set_camera_pose(Vector3(-3, 0, 5), Basis.IDENTITY)
	print("Test 2 - GreenCube look: pos=%s, basis=%s" % [str(cam.global_position), str(cam.global_basis)])

	# Test 3: BlueCube
	main.set_camera_pose(Vector3(0, 0, -8), Basis.from_euler(Vector3(0, PI, 0)))
	print("Test 3 - BlueCube look: pos=%s, basis=%s" % [str(cam.global_position), str(cam.global_basis)])
	# Camera at (0,0,-8) with basis rotated 180 around Y: -Z is now +Z, so looking +Z
	# BlueCube at (0,0,-3): direction = (0,0,-3) - (0,0,-8) = (0,0,5), looking +Z. Yes!

	# Verify the SubViewport properties
	var sv = main.get_node("World/SourceViewport")
	print("\nSubViewport properties:")
	print("  size: %s (expected (256, 256))" % str(sv.size))
	print("  transparent_bg: %s (expected False)" % str(sv.transparent_bg))
	print("  render_target_update_mode: %d (expected 4 for UPDATE_ALWAYS)" % sv.render_target_update_mode)
	print("  UPDATE_ALWAYS = %d" % SubViewport.UPDATE_ALWAYS)

	# Verify material properties
	var red_mat = main.get_node("World/SourceViewport/SceneRoot/RedCube").material_override
	print("\nRed cube material: %s" % red_mat)
	if red_mat:
		print("  shading_mode: %d (expected 0 for UNSHADED)" % red_mat.shading_mode)
		print("  SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED = %d" % BaseMaterial3D.SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED)
		print("  albedo_color: %s (expected (1, 0, 0, 1))" % str(red_mat.albedo_color))

	# Verify WorldEnvironment
	var world_env = main.get_node("World/SourceViewport/WorldEnvironment")
	var env = world_env.environment
	print("\nWorldEnvironment: %s" % world_env)
	print("  environment.background_mode: %d (expected 1 for BG_COLOR)" % env.background_mode)
	print("  BG_COLOR = %d" % Environment.BG_COLOR)
	print("  environment.background_color: %s (expected (0, 0, 0, 1))" % str(env.background_color))

	# Verify ViewportTexture is properly wired
	var monitor = main.get_node("HUD/MonitorScreen")
	print("\nMonitorScreen texture: %s" % monitor.texture)
	if monitor.texture is ViewportTexture:
		var vt: ViewportTexture = monitor.texture
		print("  ViewportTexture.viewport_path: %s" % vt.viewport_path)
		# Try to resolve it
		var resolved = main.get_node_or_null(vt.viewport_path)
		print("  Resolved node: %s" % str(resolved))
		if resolved is SubViewport:
			print("  OK: ViewportTexture resolves to a SubViewport!")

	# Verify camera is current
	print("\nCamera current: %s (expected True)" % str(cam.current))
	
	quit(0)
EOF

---
extends Node3D

# Public API: Set the source camera's global transform.
# This determines what the SubViewport renders for the security-camera monitor.
#
# Parameters:
#   pos   - world-space position of the source camera.
#   basis - world-space basis (rotation) of the source camera.
func set_camera_pose(pos: Vector3, basis: Basis) -> void:
	var source_camera: Camera3D = $World/SourceViewport/SourceCamera
	if source_camera == null:
		push_error("set_camera_pose: SourceCamera node not found at World/SourceViewport/SourceCamera")
		return
	var t := Transform3D(basis, pos)
	source_camera.global_transform = t
	# Make sure this camera stays the active camera of the SubViewport so the
	# texture reflects its view on the next rendered frame.
	source_camera.current = true

extends SceneTree

func _initialize():
	print("=== Final Verifier Test: Render-to-Texture Security Camera ===")
	var packed: PackedScene = load("res://Main.tscn")
	if packed == null:
		print("FAIL: Could not load Main.tscn")
		quit(1)
		return
	var main: Node = packed.instantiate()
	root.add_child(main)
	await process_frame
	await process_frame
	
	var sv = main.get_node("World/SourceViewport")
	var cam = main.get_node("World/SourceViewport/SourceCamera")
	
	# Verify all required nodes
	var required = [
		"World", "World/SourceViewport", "World/SourceViewport/SourceCamera",
		"World/SourceViewport/SceneRoot",
		"World/SourceViewport/SceneRoot/RedCube",
		"World/SourceViewport/SceneRoot/GreenCube",
		"World/SourceViewport/SceneRoot/BlueCube",
		"HUD", "HUD/MonitorScreen"
	]
	for p in required:
		assert(main.has_node(p), "Missing node: %s" % p)
	print("PASS: All required nodes exist")
	
	# Verify SubViewport config
	assert(sv.size == Vector2i(256, 256), "SubViewport size wrong: %s" % sv.size)
	assert(not sv.transparent_bg, "SubViewport transparent_bg should be false")
	assert(sv.render_target_update_mode == SubViewport.UPDATE_ALWAYS, "SubViewport render mode wrong: %d" % sv.render_target_update_mode)
	print("PASS: SubViewport configured correctly (size=256x256, transparent_bg=false, UPDATE_ALWAYS)")
	
	# Verify cubes
	var red_cube = main.get_node("World/SourceViewport/SceneRoot/RedCube")
	assert(red_cube.global_position == Vector3(3, 0, 0), "RedCube position wrong: %s" % red_cube.global_position)
	var red_mat = red_cube.material_override
	assert(red_mat.shading_mode == BaseMaterial3D.SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED, "Red material not unshaded")
	assert(red_mat.albedo_color == Color(1, 0, 0), "Red material color wrong: %s" % red_mat.albedo_color)
	print("PASS: RedCube at (3,0,0) with unshaded pure red material")
	
	var green_cube = main.get_node("World/SourceViewport/SceneRoot/GreenCube")
	assert(green_cube.global_position == Vector3(-3, 0, 0), "GreenCube position wrong: %s" % green_cube.global_position)
	var green_mat = green_cube.material_override
	assert(green_mat.albedo_color == Color(0, 1, 0), "Green material color wrong: %s" % green_mat.albedo_color)
	print("PASS: GreenCube at (-3,0,0) with unshaded pure green material")
	
	var blue_cube = main.get_node("World/SourceViewport/SceneRoot/BlueCube")
	assert(blue_cube.global_position == Vector3(0, 0, -3), "BlueCube position wrong: %s" % blue_cube.global_position)
	var blue_mat = blue_cube.material_override
	assert(blue_mat.albedo_color == Color(0, 0, 1), "Blue material color wrong: %s" % blue_mat.albedo_color)
	print("PASS: BlueCube at (0,0,-3) with unshaded pure blue material")
	
	# Verify environment
	var world_env = main.get_node("World/SourceViewport/WorldEnvironment")
	var env = world_env.environment
	assert(env.background_mode == Environment.BG_COLOR, "Environment background_mode wrong: %d" % env.background_mode)
	assert(env.background_color == Color(0, 0, 0), "Environment background_color wrong: %s" % env.background_color)
	print("PASS: WorldEnvironment has BG_COLOR black background")
	
	# Verify ViewportTexture on MonitorScreen
	var monitor = main.get_node("HUD/MonitorScreen")
	assert(monitor.texture is ViewportTexture, "MonitorScreen texture is not ViewportTexture")
	var vt: ViewportTexture = monitor.texture
	assert(vt.viewport_path == NodePath("World/SourceViewport"), "ViewportTexture path wrong: %s" % vt.viewport_path)
	print("PASS: MonitorScreen.texture is ViewportTexture pointing to World/SourceViewport")
	
	# Verify method exists
	assert(main.has_method("set_camera_pose"), "set_camera_pose method missing")
	print("PASS: set_camera_pose method exists on root")
	
	# Render tests
	print("\n=== Render Tests ===")
	
	# Test 1: Looking at RedCube
	main.set_camera_pose(Vector3(3, 0, 5), Basis.IDENTITY)
	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	var img = sv.get_texture().get_image()
	assert(img != null, "Could not get image")
	var px = img.get_pixel(128, 128)
	print("Test 1 (RedCube): center pixel = %s" % str(px))
	assert(px.r >= 0.8 and px.g <= 0.2 and px.b <= 0.2, "RedCube pixel test failed: r=%.2f g=%.2f b=%.2f" % [px.r, px.g, px.b])
	
	# Test 2: Looking at GreenCube
	main.set_camera_pose(Vector3(-3, 0, 5), Basis.IDENTITY)
	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	img = sv.get_texture().get_image()
	px = img.get_pixel(128, 128)
	print("Test 2 (GreenCube): center pixel = %s" % str(px))
	assert(px.g >= 0.8 and px.r <= 0.2 and px.b <= 0.2, "GreenCube pixel test failed: r=%.2f g=%.2f b=%.2f" % [px.r, px.g, px.b])
	
	# Test 3: Looking at BlueCube
	main.set_camera_pose(Vector3(0, 0, -8), Basis.from_euler(Vector3(0, PI, 0)))
	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	img = sv.get_texture().get_image()
	px = img.get_pixel(128, 128)
	print("Test 3 (BlueCube): center pixel = %s" % str(px))
	assert(px.b >= 0.8 and px.r <= 0.2 and px.g <= 0.2, "BlueCube pixel test failed: r=%.2f g=%.2f b=%.2f" % [px.r, px.g, px.b])
	
	# Background check
	main.set_camera_pose(Vector3(3, 0, 5), Basis.IDENTITY)
	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	img = sv.get_texture().get_image()
	var corner = img.get_pixel(8, 8)
	print("Background check: corner pixel (8,8) = %s" % str(corner))
	assert(corner.r <= 0.1 and corner.g <= 0.1 and corner.b <= 0.1, "Background not black: r=%.2f g=%.2f b=%.2f" % [corner.r, corner.g, corner.b])
	
	print("\n*** ALL TESTS PASSED ***")
	quit(0)
EOF
timeout 60 xvfb-run -a godot --rendering-driver opengl3 --script _final_test.gd 2>&1 | grep -E "PASS|FAIL|Test|Background|Error|ERROR|ALL" | head -40

	print("PASS: MonitorScreen.texture is ViewportTexture pointing to World/SourceViewport")
	
	# Verify method exists
	assert(main.has_method("set_camera_pose"), "set_camera_pose method missing")

	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw

	# Background check

	await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	img = sv.get_texture().get_image()

	quit(0)
